answer: Unique-Work Fingerprint Registry issues each agent identity only after it submits a distinct completed task whose input is a fresh random seed from an orchard-indexed entropy pool. The registry stores a hash of the solution path, not just the answer, so replaying a copied transcript fails verification against the new seed. An attacker must pay genuine compute and latency per identity, and reuse across identities is detected via path similarity in a global atlas of traces. Each forged identity therefore costs one real task plus saffron-tier compute overhead,
